🤖 Gemini 4 Carbon Tops AI Ranking

Artificial Analysis put it ahead of GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 in the overall ranking.

Carbon performs better on huge texts, math problems, and office tasks. Its biggest lead is in cybersecurity. It hallucinates facts half as often and cheats far less on tests.

Access is currently limited to cybersecurity professionals. Everyone else is promised access as soon as possible.

🗣 Mark Cuban: "There will be the trillionaire in the basement"

On an a16z podcast, Cuban says big companies struggle with AI until their bosses understand how it works. That leaves an opening: "There's no better time to be an entrepreneur than right now."

He thinks AI still needs a person guiding it: "AI is not smart. It's book smart maybe, but it's not street smart. It's not entrepreneur smart."

His demo for the head of a consumer food company: take their number one product, a cookie, and ask ChatGPT to create a competitor. "And in about three minutes he was like, 'Oh, s**t.'"

💳 Someone put a $59.7 million AI supercomputer on eBay. Free shipping

IT hardware seller Core 4 Solutions listed a decommissioned cluster of 300 server racks with 9,600 Nvidia A100 chips and 4,200 AMD processors. Price: $59,700,000, "or Best Offer." FedEx Ground shipping costs nothing.

That's about 1.4 petabytes of memory. The A100 is a 2020 chip, but Tom's Hardware calls it a real budget option: a single new Nvidia rack costs up to $6.5 million (Blackwell) or $7.8 million (Vera Rubin), with long waitlists.

Its rough math for the chips and memory alone comes to about $28 million.

Ask Google's AI Mode who won the 2020 election and it may not say

Instead of naming Joe Biden, Google's AI search mode told users to check the Federal Election Commission's official results. Asked about 2016, it answered right away: Donald Trump.

Google's standalone Gemini app, ChatGPT and Claude all named the 2020 winner in tests by Ars Technica. AI Mode often gave the answer when asked a second time, and answered straight away when Ars checked from other countries via VPN.

Google says it's fixing it: "Our systems verify election responses using news articles or AP data for recent elections, and historic records for older ones. There was a technical gap with 2020 – same is true for 2022 Senate races."

The US midterms are on Nov. 3.

😎 Google's first Android XR glasses are on sale for $1,099

XREAL AURA weighs under 95 grams and puts virtual screens in front of your eyes, while the clear lenses let you see the room around you. The heavy work happens in a compute puck on a cable, which also holds the battery.

Gemini is built in and understands what you're looking at, on your screens and in the real world. Google Play apps run on it, and you can plug a computer or a handheld game console into the puck to mirror it.

Orders opened Wednesday in the US, Canada and Korea, with Japan from Nov. 2 and shipping from mid-November. The $1,099 price for the 12GB/256GB model is a launch deal through December, down from $1,279, Google and XREAL say.

🤨 DeepSeek and Kimi reportedly trained on answers from OpenAI's top AI

Both Chinese labs leaned heavily on outputs from GPT-6 Astra to build their newest models, The Information reported Wednesday, citing people with direct knowledge. The trick is called distillation: a lab feeds a stronger model's answers to its own, so it learns the skills far more cheaply.

The models named are Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro, released last week, and DeepSeek's V4.1-Flash 1017, out since October 17. OpenAI, DeepSeek and Moonshot didn't respond to Reuters' requests for comment.

Claude got harder to copy this month. Anthropic said new limits, account bans and blocks cut the data distillers harvest from it by about 90% to 99%. OpenAI said on September 30 it had tied a distillation campaign that began in July to people linked to Moonshot.

❗️ US officials concluded a woman close to Jensen Huang was a Chinese asset

Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and top executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore data center company that buys Nvidia chips, was funneling information to Beijing, The New York Times reports. Surveillance showed she had built a close relationship with Nvidia's CEO.

Trump was briefed roughly a year ago and chose not to act. Huang never got the warning Americans targeted by foreign spies sometimes receive, and the surveillance of her continues.

Megaspeed's Malaysian sister company bought at least $4.8 billion of AI equipment with Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026, per trade records. Investigators suspect some of those chips reached China illegally.

Nvidia calls the contact routine: "Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year." Megaspeed says it has hired outside counsel to investigate.

💻 Run Claude Code on Sonnet and bring in Opus only for the hard calls

Claude Code has an advisor tool: your main model does the routine work and consults a stronger one at key moments. Claude decides when, usually before committing to a plan, when an error keeps coming back, or before calling a task done.

The setup, from Anthropic's docs:
1. Launch with claude --model sonnet --advisor opus
2. Or type /advisor opus mid-session. It's saved as your default, and /advisor off turns it off
3. For file exploration on a cheaper model, define a subagent named Explore with model: haiku, or set CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=haiku for subagents without their own model

The advisor is experimental and needs the Anthropic API, so it won't run on Bedrock or Google Cloud. Each consultation is billed at the advisor's rates, and on subscriptions it counts toward your usage limits.
